intro.title: HOC withAuth
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable Higher-Order Component (HOC) called `withAuth` that protects certain React components, ensuring only authenticated users can access them. You will learn the core concept of a HOC, which is a function that takes a component and returns a new, enhanced component with additional logic. The main technologies involved are React for building UI components and TypeScript for adding type safety to your props and component structure. By the end, you will have a functional `withAuth` HOC that checks for user authentication and conditionally renders the wrapped component or a redirect.
intro.usecase: Higher-Order Components like withAuth are essential for implementing authentication guards in real-world React applications. You'll see this pattern in admin dashboards where certain routes or components should only be accessible to logged-in users with specific permissions. For example, an e-commerce platform might use withAuth to protect the checkout page, user profile editor, or order history panel. This pattern also appears in SaaS products where different subscription tiers get access to different features—basic users might see limited functionality while premium users see the full dashboard. Implementing withAuth helps developers centralize authentication logic and keep components focused on their primary responsibilities.
